decisions.rationale: Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Packet binding and actor-envelope contracts concern adjacent metadata identity, but they do not own FileSafe operation values carried in ExecutionRequest.env_vars.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Shared projection health and generic GUI-oracle gaps are neighbors, but none owns the FileSafe metrics projection's freshness, redaction, empty/error, accessibility, localization, and scale semantics.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Blocked-episode identity and approval-scope contracts are adjacent owner contracts; the anchor is specifically FileSafe's non-competing authority and Decision Policy delegation boundary.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Bounded predicate regex policy and shell execution are adjacent command-safety concerns, but neither defines FileSafe full-command regex anchoring and multiline or NUL boundary semantics.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Pre-dispatch blocker and provider-identity checks are adjacent ordering contracts, but they do not define FileSafe startup validation and runner-construction order.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Catalog reload and concurrent cache recovery are neighboring lifecycle patterns, but neither governs FileSafe bundled and local destructive-pattern parsing, atomic reload, or fail-closed fallback.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Template reparsing and shell-injection execution are related command interpretation risks, but they do not define FileSafe's normalized full-command identity.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Actor envelopes, domain approvals, and packet bindings are adjacent trust boundaries, but none owns authorization to set FileSafe gate/interview operation classifications.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Misread recovery acknowledgement and unverified provider identity are analogous truthful-state failures, but they have different authorities, lifecycles, state boundaries, and failure semantics.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Include containment, package-file safety, and frozen-cwd invalidation are neighboring path controls; none is the FileSafe empty-allowlist write-scope contract.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Parent ceilings and contextual approval reuse are adjacent anti-widening controls, but they do not own the retired-versus-live FileSafe environment-override authority conflict.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Provider-profile isolation, caller-scoped capability, and shared-context visibility are neighbors, but none defines immutable per-request scope isolation for shared FileSafe guard objects.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Approval non-widening, target binding, and reuse are related, but they do not resolve the FileSafe checklist's verification-gate exemption and missing current override receipt.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Requested/effective provider identity, auth resolution, and readiness predicates are adjacent, but none defines the Security Lane required-model decision payload, mismatch block, recovery, and mid-run loss behavior.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Generic GUI wiring, UI-oracle, and approval-accessibility gaps are neighbors, but none owns the canonical side-panel shell's responsive reference-layout and accessibility behavior.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Shared projection health, event persistence, and recovery-oracle contracts are adjacent; none is the FileSafe GUI config save/apply/restart plus seglog projection lifecycle.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Unverified identity, misleading recovery, and pre-dispatch blockers are analogous fail-closed concerns, but none governs zero-pattern FileSafe guard initialization.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Vision lineage, adversarial OCR handling, and caller-scoped permission evaluation are adjacent, but none defines the FileSafe image-source grant lifetime, recency, cancellation, redaction decision, and provider disclosure protocol.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. The comparator bridges are retired Commands and BinaryLocator authorities; they are only structurally analogous and are not the retired FileSafe F2-001 bridge.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Path containment, local-output cleanup, and cwd invalidation are neighbors, but none resolves privileged FileSafe cleanup versus write-scope precedence and partial-failure evidence.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Executor pre-dispatch blocker resolution and approval revalidation are adjacent ordering contracts, but neither is the FileSafe Platform/BaseRunner two-stage prompt, context, and final-command check.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Normalized field preservation is adjacent, but it has a different provider-facade authority and lifecycle from preserving GuiConfig.filesafe's three guard configs and approved_commands.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Index routing, consumer deference, and cross-cutting contract ownership are neighboring authority patterns, but none is FileSafe's accepted safety-policy ownership and non-node-generation boundary.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Clipboard bridge policy and immutable or replay-safe approvals are adjacent, but the anchor combines a distinct Final GUI approval/clipboard/LSP lifecycle boundary.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Shared-core and cross-surface ownership splits are related architecture boundaries, but concrete GUI module layout is neither of those product authorities nor a security lifecycle contract.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. No comparator addresses the same LSP startup, operation, teardown, recovery, user outcome, and failure boundary; vocabulary-adjacent diagnostics were insufficient.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Shared untrusted-input limits and artifact trust/privacy are adjacent, but neither owns external GUI drag-and-drop platform ingestion behavior.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Teacher navigation races are a plausible interaction neighbor, but they do not share the authority, lifecycle, state boundary, or failures of GUI mid-stream steering.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. The browser owner and stale-canon boundary is adjacent to browser presentation, but it is not the Final GUI webview embedding conflict risk.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Structured diagnostics and sensitive debug-evidence lifecycle are neighbors, but neither is the DAP debugger reliability lifecycle and user-visible failure contract.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Remote-helper SSH authenticity is adjacent to SSH transport, but it does not cover the Final GUI SSH connection stability lifecycle and recovery behavior.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Catalog provenance/update lifecycle and live capability-discovery failure are neighbors, but neither is the GUI catalog availability and recovery contract.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Typed notification sound destinations are adjacent audio behavior, but they do not own Final GUI sound-effects playback, failure, and accessibility risk.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Secure raw-document validation and trusted import activation are adjacent theme-ingestion concerns, but neither is the Final GUI custom-theme validation lifecycle.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. No comparator governs the same Settings information architecture, tab-count constraints, responsive behavior, and user outcome; generic GUI observations were too broad to list.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Concurrent cache correctness is a plausible reload-performance dependency, but it has a different BinaryLocator authority and failure boundary from GUI project switching.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Global resource ceilings are a plausible neighbor, but they do not own file-watcher lifecycle, project switching, resource exhaustion, and visible recovery behavior.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Concurrent cache recovery and provider failure semantics are neighboring backpressure patterns, but neither owns the visualizer host bridge's concurrency and feedback transport.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Trusted imports, plugin isolation, and script-free predicates are adjacent execution-safety controls, but none is the visualizer theme and third-party library default-deny contract.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Trace persistence, artifact privacy, and debug-evidence lifecycle are adjacent audit-data contracts, but none owns visualizer-specific audit metadata creation, retention, and deletion.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Cross-cutting ownership, domain approval binding, and compatibility non-widening are adjacent, but none is the Permissions System's explicit visualizer/persona/web-session policy authority.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Approval lifetime, replay, TOCTOU, revalidation, and stale-action contracts are close neighbors; the anchor remains distinct because it governs web-session approval-card race and stale-card UI semantics.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Persona profile ceilings and persona/blocked-action projections are adjacent, but they do not state the approval-card prohibition on mutating Persona profiles.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Requested/effective identity, persona projections, and visible trust disclosure are neighboring presentation contracts, but none is Persona-specific progressive disclosure.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Trusted import activation and catalog provenance are neighbors, but curated third-party visualizer library records have a distinct owner, artifact lifecycle, and execution outcome.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Shared projection-health vocabulary and generic GUI truth are adjacent, but neither owns inline visualizer v2 feedback-state parity.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Provider, source-control, auth-resolution, and cross-cutting owner maps are adjacent; none is GitHub API authentication's authoritative realm and consumer-obligation boundary.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Secret-store failure oracles, credential custody, and the shared OAuth lifecycle are close neighbors, but none defines GitHub auth behavior when the OS credential store is absent, locked, corrupt, or intermittent.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Source-control and provider/shell ownership splits are adjacent, but they do not reproduce the Git, GitHub hosting, Copilot, SSH transport, and FileSafe authority partition.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Browser-login polling, WebSocket replay defense, and the general OAuth lifecycle are adjacent; none owns GitHub's loopback callback correlation, replay defense, listener lifecycle, and recovery.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Auth resolution boundaries are adjacent to host selection, but they do not select GitHub's operative host-policy state set or close its conditional MVP policy.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Requested/effective identity, identity privacy, propagation, and account-switch invalidation are neighbors, but none owns GitHub account_id and credential_ref creation, rotation, revocation, merge, deletion, and tombstoning.

Exhaustive comparison against all 219 comparators found no merge-equivalent feature. Account-switch invalidation and generic truthful GUI disclosure are adjacent, but none defines GitHub account-switch reason copy, redaction, loading/error, accessibility, localization, and acceptance oracles.
